title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
authors: Kentaro Nakajo, Hojun Im, Keiichiro Nishimura, Masahiro Teraoka, Masaya Kikuchi
abstract: While graphene/n-type silicon (Gr/n-Si) and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si solar cells offer a cost-effective alternative to conventional photovoltaics, achieving simultaneous high power conversion efficiency (PCE) and long-term environmental stability remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report the synergistic enhancement of both performance and stability in a planar trilayer PEDOT:PSS/Gr/n-Si Schottky junction architecture. By systematically benchmarking this hybrid device against pristine Gr/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells fabricated on untextured substrates, we isolate the fundamental optoelectronic and barrier functions of the carbon lattice. Comprehensive analyses reveal that the PEDOT:PSS layer simultaneously functions as an anti-reflection coating, a moderate p-type dopant for the underlying graphene, and a conductivity enhancer, collectively optimizing interfacial charge transport. Consequently, the trilayer device achieves a PCE of 8.52%, markedly outperforming the pristine Gr/n-Si reference cell (4.56%). Crucially, the atomic impermeability of the graphene sheet serves as a robust environmental barrier. While bare PEDOT:PSS/n-Si junctions retained only ~29% of their initial efficiency after 75 days of ambient exposure, graphene shields the active junction from moisture-induced degradation of the hygroscopic PEDOT:PSS overlayer. This enables the trilayer device to retain approximately 90% of its initial efficiency over the same 75-day period. The complementary roles of graphene as both a highly crystalline charge transport interface and an impermeable protective barrier establish a highly effective strategy for engineering high-efficiency, environmentally stable hybrid photovoltaics.

infographic.key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-Si trilayer combines improved photovoltaic efficiency with graphene-mediated protection against environmental degradation.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The planar architecture offers a route to more efficient, durable hybrid silicon solar cells without substrate texturing.
method: Benchmark trilayer cells against graphene/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si references on untextured substrates.
Use PEDOT:PSS for anti-reflection, moderate graphene p-doping, and enhanced conductivity.
Use graphene as a charge-transport interface and moisture barrier.
infographic.evidence_signal: The trilayer achieved 8.52% PCE versus 4.56% for graphene/n-Si and retained approximately 90% of its initial efficiency after 75 days in ambient conditions, versus approximately 29% for PEDOT:PSS/n-Si.
infographic.watch_item: The reported 75-day ambient exposure does not establish long-term outdoor durability or standardized accelerated-aging performance.
infographic.paper_title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells

title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
authors: Sofiia Kosar, Anil R. Pininti, Vladyslav Hnapovskyi, José P. Jurado, Subhashri Mannar, Lorenzo Mardegan
abstract: The scalable fabrication of high-quality, large-area perovskite thin films is hindered by microscopic inhomogeneities, particularly residual compositional impurities formed during processing. Identifying these impurities, understanding their impact on device operation, and enabling their rapid detection are essential for upscaling perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Here, nano-Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy combined with high-resolution optical and scanning probe techniques was used to identify detrimental impurities in wide-bandgap perovskite films relevant to tandem solar cells. Photo-stress experiments revealed that degradation of the perovskite layer initiates at impurity-perovskite interfaces, demonstrating that impurities act as failure nucleation sites. Leveraging these insights, a rapid, non-invasive, and high-throughput framework based on high-resolution reflected light microscopy and machine learning-supported image analysis was developed, enabling detection and quantification of harmful impurities in as-prepared films within seconds. Films with higher impurity density show accelerated early degradation, establishing this parameter as an early-warning metric for stability screening. Extending this framework to degradation tracking further reveals coupled photo- and thermo-chemical contributions to impurity-mediated instability. Overall, this work establishes a practical chemically-validated diagnostic imaging framework for rapid pre-screening of perovskite films to enable stable and scalable PSCs.

infographic.key_insight: Microscopic impurities seed perovskite degradation, and machine learning-supported optical imaging can rapidly flag films at higher risk.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Fast, non-invasive impurity screening could support quality control for scalable, stable perovskite solar cells.
method: Identify impurities using nano-FTIR spectroscopy and high-resolution optical and scanning probe techniques.
Use photo-stress experiments to locate degradation initiation sites.
Detect and quantify impurities within seconds using reflected-light microscopy and machine learning-supported image analysis.
infographic.evidence_signal: Photo-stress tests linked degradation onset to impurity–perovskite interfaces, while films with higher impurity density showed faster early degradation.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract does not report detection accuracy or validation across different film compositions and manufacturing conditions.
infographic.paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells

title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics
authors: Qiwei Han, Chi Zhou
abstract: Machine-learning models for perovskite solar cells are typically evaluated using random data splits, which we show systematically leak information through massive internal duplication. Because nearly two-thirds of curated devices share their exact recipe with another, random splits primarily reward the mere recall of historical data rather than testing true physical generalisation. To solve this, we mapped the institutional provenance of the Perovskite Database and established a rigorous hierarchy of grouped splits that progressively isolate duplicate devices, publications, and institutions. Benchmarking thirteen models establishes new state-of-the-art performance across all splits and reveals a critical regime shift: while tree ensembles dominate random splits by recognising familiar recipes, their ranking collapses on genuinely unseen institutions and future discoveries, where composition-aware neural architectures excel. Furthermore, feature importance demonstrates that the device architecture and fabrication methodology dictate final efficiency just as strongly as the absorber chemistry. This standardised protocol empowers the community to separate memorisation from true physical discovery.

infographic.key_insight: Random splits reward memorisation of duplicated perovskite device recipes, while provenance-grouped evaluation reveals which models generalise beyond familiar data.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Evaluating models on unseen institutions and future discoveries better tests their usefulness for guiding new solar-cell designs and fabrication choices.
method: Map institutional provenance in the Perovskite Database.
Progressively isolate duplicate devices, publications and institutions using grouped splits.
Benchmark 13 models and analyse the importance of chemistry, architecture and fabrication features.
infographic.evidence_signal: Nearly two-thirds of curated devices share an exact recipe with another; tree ensembles lead on random splits, but composition-aware neural models excel on unseen institutions and future discoveries.
infographic.watch_item: Reliable implementation requires accurate recipe matching and provenance metadata; the abstract provides no numerical performance margins.
infographic.paper_title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics

title: A Hybrid TFT-NBEATS Framework for Robust Multi-Horizon Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
authors: Shafi Bin Sultan, Sabik Bin Sultan, Mohammad Tajrian Arafat Alvi, Rayhanul Islam Sony, Abdulah Al Numan
abstract: Accurate multi-horizon photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is essential for grid stability, energy scheduling, and the efficient operation of PVbatterygrid systems. However, existing models often fail to jointly capture short-term variability and long-term temporal patterns, while lacking unified multi-horizon capability and interpretability. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel hybrid deep learning framework that integrates a Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) and N-BEATS within an attention-based fusion architecture. The proposed model leverages TFT to learn short-term temporal dependencies and dynamic feature importance, while N-BEATS captures long-term trend and seasonal components through interpretable basis decomposition. An adaptive attention mechanism dynamically fuses both branches, enabling balanced multi-scale learning. The framework simultaneously generates forecasts for 30-minute, 2-hour, 6-hour, 12-hour, and 24-hour horizons within a single unified pipeline. The model is evaluated using multi-year real-world datasets from the Desert Knowledge Australia Solar Centre (DKASC). Experimental results demonstrate superior performance over statistical, machine learning, and deep learning baselines. The proposed model achieves RMSE values of 42.35, 46.27, 52.29, and 48.11 across the 20162017, 2023, 2024, and 20252026 datasets, respectively, corresponding to a 3540% reduction compared to the best baseline (TFT). Additionally, MAPE remains below 5% across all datasets, indicating high predictive accuracy and stability. The model also provides interpretability through attention visualization and trendseasonality decomposition, and is deployed on a cloud-based platform for real-time forecasting. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework is robust, interpretable, and suitable for practical renewable energy applications.

infographic.key_insight: A hybrid TFT–N-BEATS model combines short-term dynamics with long-term patterns to improve multi-horizon photovoltaic power forecasting.
infographic.engineering_relevance: More accurate PV forecasts can support grid stability, energy scheduling, and coordinated PV–battery–grid operation.
method: TFT learns short-term dependencies and dynamic feature importance.
N-BEATS decomposes long-term trends and seasonality.
Adaptive attention fuses both branches for five forecast horizons from 30 minutes to 24 hours.
infographic.evidence_signal: On multi-year DKASC datasets, the abstract reports RMSE values of 42.35–52.29, a 35–40% reduction versus TFT, and MAPE below 5% across datasets.
infographic.watch_item: RMSE units and horizon-specific results are not specified in the abstract, limiting assessment of operational accuracy.
infographic.paper_title: A Hybrid TFT-NBEATS Framework for Robust Multi-Horizon Photovoltaic Power Forecasting

title: Benchmark for Structured Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Perovskite Photovoltaics
authors: Qiwei Han, Chi Zhou, Gaoxiang Yuan
abstract: While retrieval-augmented language models increasingly serve as literature assistants in the physical sciences, existing benchmarks evaluate them primarily on qualitative text overlap or through model-based scoring rather than against verified experimental ground truth. In experimental materials disciplines such as perovskite photovoltaics, however, the most critical inquiries are inherently quantitative and aggregate measurements across dozens or hundreds of papers. Here, we present a quantitative question-answering benchmark where all 755 ground-truth answers are computed directly from 45,441 measured device records (40,889 human-curated records through 2021 and 4,552 records extracted from 2022-2026 literature). Benchmarking six retrieval architectures over 158,274 passages from 25,662 papers using an open 14B model on a single 24 GB GPU, standard passage retrieval tops out at 16-23% accuracy (compared to 1.6-6.5% zero-shot). In contrast, equipping the language model with read-only SQL execution over the structured device table elevates accuracy to 51.5% on historical and 50.8% on prospective literature -- a 33.01.8 percentage-point advantage over hybrid text retrieval. Aggregate queries spanning extrema, distributions, and filtered record counts prove virtually unsolvable via text retrieval alone, demonstrating that systematic table extraction is an operational prerequisite for literature-scale quantitative inquiry.

infographic.key_insight: Giving a language model read-only SQL access to structured perovskite device data raised quantitative question-answering accuracy to about 51%, versus 16–23% for standard passage retrieval.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Reliable literature-scale comparisons of solar-cell measurements require structured experimental records, not text retrieval alone.
method: Compute 755 ground-truth answers from 45,441 measured device records.
Benchmark six retrieval architectures over 158,274 passages from 25,662 papers.
Evaluate an open 14B model with read-only SQL access on a single 24 GB GPU.
infographic.evidence_signal: SQL-enabled accuracy reached 51.5% on historical literature and 50.8% on prospective literature, while zero-shot accuracy ranged from 1.6% to 6.5%.
infographic.watch_item: Structured retrieval depends on accurate table extraction and still leaves roughly half of benchmark questions unanswered correctly.
infographic.paper_title: Benchmark for Structured Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Perovskite Photovoltaics

title: Universal Synthesis of Large-Area Hybrid Perovskite Monolayers Enabling Lithography-Free, Low-Static-Power Optoelectronics
authors: Shankeerthan Kalyanasundaram, Swarit Dwivedi, Sanje Mahasivam, Christopher R. McNeill, Sudha Mokkapati
abstract: Solution-phase synthesis of monolayer hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites is constrained by rapid out-of-plane crystal growth, uncontrolled nucleation, and strong interlayer aggregation, yielding flakes of only a few μm. We introduce a steric-engineering ternary-solvent growth strategy to synthesize monolayer and few-layer A2MX4 hybrid perovskites with exceptionally large surface areas. By combining alcohol cosolvents with an amine additive, out-of-plane stacking is suppressed. Using (PEA)2CuCl4 as a model system, monolayers with lateral areas exceeding 1000 μm2 are achieved, representing a massive dimensional increase over conventional methods. Molecular dynamics and quantum-chemical calculations show that longer-chain alcohols reorganize precursor solvation, while solvent volatility prolongs edge-mediated precursor transport during annealing. This strategy demonstrates universal applicability across diverse organic spacer cations (PEA+, F-PEA+, PentA+), metal centers (Cu2+, Mn2+, Pb2+), and halides (Cl-, Br-, I-). The large lateral dimensions enable direct, solvent-free electrical contact fabrication via physical shadow masking, bypassing chemical degradation from solvents used in conventional lithography. Planar devices fabricated from isolated ultrathin (PEA)2PbI4 channels exhibit ultra-low dark currents down to the 10^-15 - 10^-13 A range, enabling femtowatt-to-picowatt static power consumption, ~ 0.2 pW at 5 V, a 250-fold reduction relative to drop-cast films, while maintaining a high light-to-dark current ratio of 4.3 x 102. This work establishes precise steric and solvation control as a paradigm for scalable, compositionally diverse, low-static-power monolayer 2D perovskite optoelectronics.

infographic.key_insight: A ternary-solvent growth strategy produces large-area hybrid perovskite monolayers, enabling lithography-free optoelectronic devices with ultra-low static power.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Large isolated flakes support solvent-free shadow-mask contacts, avoiding solvent-induced lithography damage while reducing standby power.
method: Combine alcohol cosolvents with an amine additive to suppress out-of-plane stacking.
Tune precursor solvation and annealing transport to promote lateral growth.

infographic.paper_title: Universal Synthesis of Large-Area Hybrid Perovskite Monolayers Enabling Lithography-Free, Low-Static-Power Optoelectronics

title: Vision Transformers for Estimating Irradiance Using Data Scarce Sky Images
authors: David Hamlyn, Sunny Chaudhary, Tasmiat Rahman
abstract: Accurate estimation of diffuse horizontal irradiance (DHI) is critical for optimising photovoltaic system performance and energy forecasting yet remains challenging in regions lacking comprehensive ground-based instrumentation. Recent advancements using Vision Transformers (ViTs) trained on extensive sky image datasets have shown promise in replacing costly irradiance measurement equipment, but the scarcity of long-term, high-quality sky imagery significantly restricts practical implementation. Addressing this critical gap, this study proposes a novel dual-framework approach designed for data-scarce scenarios. First, calculated atmospheric parameters, including extraterrestrial irradiance and cyclic time encodings, are integrated to represent sky conditions without utilising any instrumentation. Next, a sequential pipeline initially predicts synthetic global horizontal irradiance (GHI) and uses it as a feature, to refine DHI estimation. Finally, a dual-parallel architecture simultaneously processes raw and overlay-enhanced fisheye sky images. Overlays are generated through unsupervised, physics-informed cloud segmentation to highlight dynamic sky features. Empirical validation is performed using data from the Chilbolton Observatory, chosen for its temperate climate and frequent cloud variability. To simulate data-scarce conditions, models are trained on a single month (e.g., January) and evaluated across a temporally disjoint, full-year test set. Under this setup, the sequential and dual-parallel frameworks achieve RMSE values within 2-3 W/m^2 and 1-6 W/m^2, respectively, of a state-of-the-art ViT trained on the complete dataset. By combining physics-informed modelling with unsupervised segmentation, the proposed method provides a scalable and cost-effective solution for DHI estimation, advancing solar resource assessment in data-constrained environments.

infographic.key_insight: Physics-informed Vision Transformer frameworks estimate diffuse horizontal irradiance from scarce sky imagery with RMSE close to a full-dataset ViT baseline.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce reliance on costly irradiance instrumentation for photovoltaic performance optimisation and solar energy forecasting.
method: Add calculated extraterrestrial irradiance and cyclic time features.
Use predicted global horizontal irradiance to refine diffuse irradiance estimates in a sequential pipeline.

infographic.watch_item: Validation at one temperate-climate site leaves generalisation to other climates and imaging setups unestablished.
infographic.paper_title: Vision Transformers for Estimating Irradiance Using Data Scarce Sky Images

title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
authors: Julisa Juarez, Akash Dasgupta, Alan Zhan, Lamtiur P. Samosir, David S. Ginger*
abstract: Studying real-time degradation in perovskite semiconductors remains an important challenge. Conventional methods often cannot separate interfacial and bulk processes or rely on destructive analysis. Here, we demonstrate multiwavelength excitation photoluminescence (PL) as a nondestructive approach to distinguish interface- and bulk-dominated recombination losses. Using phenethylammonium tetrafluoroborate (PEABF4) treatment as a model, we use PL to show that PEABF4 passivates the electron transport layer (ETL)/perovskite interface, reducing interfacial recombination losses from fullerene deposition. However, upon thermal aging, PEABF4-treated stacks degrade more rapidly, with recombination losses broadening from the ETL/perovskite interface into the absorber. Diffusion-recombination simulations support interpreting excitation-wavelength-dependent PL decay signatures consistent with changes in surface recombination velocity and bulk lifetime, providing a framework for depth-sensitive comparisons during aging. Collectively, these results further establish multiwavelength excitation PL as a platform for studying recombination losses during aging of perovskite films.

infographic.key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence reveals that PEABF4 treatment initially reduces interfacial recombination but accelerates degradation during thermal aging, with losses extending into the perovskite absorber.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive, nondestructive monitoring can help engineers assess whether interface passivation improves both initial performance and thermal durability.
method: Use multiple excitation wavelengths to probe depth-dependent photoluminescence responses.
Compare PEABF4-treated and untreated perovskite stacks during thermal aging.

infographic.evidence_signal: PL measurements indicate reduced recombination from fullerene deposition after treatment, followed by faster degradation during thermal aging; simulations support contributions from changing surface recombination velocity and bulk lifetime.
infographic.watch_item: Depth-dependent losses are inferred through optical measurements and modeling; the abstract provides no quantitative lifetime gains or device-efficiency validation.
infographic.paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells

title: Intensity-driven Mott-like transition in a 2D Ruddlesden-Popper perovskite
authors: Koushik Mondal, Amit Haldar, Indrajit Mondal, Arpita Dutta, Himanshu Bhatt, Biswajit Mahata
abstract: Two-dimensional Ruddlesden-Popper-type halide perovskites have emerged as promising cutting-edge nonlinear optical materials due to their strong excitonic effects and carrier-density-dependent optical responses. In this work, we investigate the nonlinear optical properties and ultrafast carrier dynamics of (BA)$_2$PbI$_4$ under infrared excitation, resonant with the two-photon energy of its excitonic transition. Using a nonlinear femtosecond Z-scan measurement with a 1030\,nm pump pulse, we observe a pronounced intensity-dependent evolution of the nonlinear absorption coefficient and the refractive index. With increasing pump intensity, a switch from saturable absorption to reverse saturable absorption emerges, suggesting an intensity-driven Mott-like transition. To elucidate the underlying carrier dynamics, intensity-dependent transient absorption spectroscopy was performed under the same excitation intensities. This reveals a long-lived charge carrier population above the estimated Mott density, reflecting a clear phase transition from an exciton-dominated regime to a dense electron-hole plasma regime. Moreover, such an intensity-driven, high, and switchable nonlinear optical response, along with a Mott-like transition under infrared pulse excitation, makes the 2D (BA)$_2$PbI$_4$ perovskites suitable for all-optical operation in the infrared regime.

infographic.key_insight: Increasing infrared excitation intensity drives a Mott-like crossover in 2D (BA)₂PbI₄ from exciton-dominated behavior toward a dense electron–hole plasma, alongside a switch from saturable to reverse saturable absorption.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The intensity-tunable optical response could support infrared all-optical switching, although the study does not demonstrate solar-cell performance gains.
method: Probe nonlinear absorption and refraction using femtosecond Z-scan measurements at 1030 nm.
Use excitation whose two-photon energy is resonant with the excitonic transition.
Track carrier dynamics with intensity-dependent transient absorption spectroscopy.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports an intensity-dependent absorption switch and a long-lived carrier population above the estimated Mott density, supporting the proposed Mott-like transition.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical switching thresholds, operational stability data, or device-level validation.
infographic.paper_title: Intensity-driven Mott-like transition in a 2D Ruddlesden-Popper perovskite

title: PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting
authors: Jelena Simeunović, Baptiste Schubnel, Pierre-Jean Alet, Pascal Frossard, Rafael E. Carrillo
abstract: Advection-diffusion plays an essential role in transport phenomena such as atmospheric and cloud dynamics. Improved forecasting of cloud motion, in turn, enhances solar power production forecasts and facilitates the integration of additional photovoltaic (PV) sources into the power grid. However, both classical numerical models and emerging deep learning approaches face challenges when applied to spatially irregular sensor networks such as those formed by weather stations. In this work, we adopt a graph signal processing perspective and model advection-diffusion particles as signals on a graph to capture the dynamics of these processes. We introduce a Physics-Informed Graph Neural Network (PING) for forecasting future advection-diffusion particle concentrations on irregular grids. The model incorporates a discretized advection-diffusion equation as a soft constraint in the loss function to guide learning toward physically consistent solutions. This model is on par with state of the art models on synthetic and real transport phenomena datasets, including sea surface temperature and cloud index datasets. Furthermore, the PING model is successfully coupled with models for forecasting PV power production. This hybrid approach leverages data fusion from ground-based sensors at PV stations and satellite images with cloud concentration to improve the accuracy of intra-day PV power production.

infographic.key_insight: PING embeds advection–diffusion physics in a graph neural network to forecast transport processes on irregular sensor networks and support solar power forecasting.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Better cloud-motion forecasts can improve intra-day photovoltaic power predictions and help integrate PV generation into the grid.
method: Represent transported particle concentrations as signals on a graph.
Use a discretized advection–diffusion equation as a soft constraint in the training loss.
Couple PING with PV forecasting models using ground-based sensor data and satellite cloud information.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports performance on par with state-of-the-art models on synthetic and real transport datasets, including sea surface temperature and cloud index data, plus improved intra-day PV forecasting.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract does not quantify PV forecasting gains, and a soft physics constraint does not guarantee physically consistent predictions.
infographic.paper_title: PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting

title: Anomalous polar chains in halide perovskites
authors: Erik Fransson, Apinya Ngoipala, Priyanka Deswal, Ethan Berger, Nicholas C. Bristowe, Paul Erhart
abstract: Local polar distortions, their collective ordering, and their field-driven reversal have been studied extensively in ferroelectric perovskites for decades. Here we identify an unusual behavior in the ferroelectric halide perovskite CsGeBr3 using large-scale molecular dynamics with first-principles-trained interatomic potentials. In its nominally cubic phase the Ge off-centering forms one-dimensional polar chains that extend over at least tens of nanometers and relax on nanosecond timescales, four orders of magnitude slower than in BaTiO3 and PbTiO3, with CsSnBr3 in between. The cubic CsGeBr3 phase is a dynamically disordered state in which oppositely polarized chains flip throughout the crystal, and a long-lived one-dimensional local polarization coexists with zero net polarization. A simple three-dimensional perovskite thus hosts long-ranged one-dimensional polar correlations with remarkably slow dynamics. In the ferroelectric phase the same chains set a one-dimensional switching mechanism, in which the polarization reverses chain by chain.

infographic.key_insight: Nominally cubic CsGeBr3 hosts long-lived, one-dimensional polar chains despite having zero net polarization.
infographic.engineering_relevance: These slow local polarization dynamics could inform halide-perovskite device modeling, although photovoltaic performance was not evaluated.
method: First-principles-trained interatomic potentials
Large-scale molecular dynamics
Analysis of polar correlations and polarization reversal
infographic.evidence_signal: Simulations reveal chains extending at least tens of nanometers and relaxing on nanosecond timescales—four orders of magnitude slower than in BaTiO3 and PbTiO3—with chain-by-chain reversal in ferroelectric CsGeBr3.
infographic.watch_item: Experimental validation and the impact of these simulated dynamics on solar-cell operation remain unestablished in the abstract.
infographic.paper_title: Anomalous polar chains in halide perovskites

title: Foundation-Style Pretraining for Scalable and Transferable Distributed PV Forecasting
authors: Dayin Chen, Xiaodan Shi, Xin Xu, Zhongyue Su, Shibo Zhu, Ruizhe Deng
abstract: The rapid growth of distributed photovoltaic (PV) generation is increasing the demand for accurate forecasting across large numbers of geographically dispersed stations. Existing approaches are commonly developed for individual sites or specific forecasting horizons, requiring repeated training and maintenance as new stations are integrated and limiting direct reuse at previously unseen sites. To address this scalability gap, this paper presents a domain-specific foundation-style pretraining framework that learns a shared forecasting model from heterogeneous multi-site and multi-horizon PV data. NWP-assisted forecasting is formulated as a sequence-completion problem that unifies historical PV power, meteorological observations, future numerical weather prediction (NWP) forecasts, and time encodings. Three pretraining objectives are designed and systematically evaluated, including forecast-aligned reconstruction, generic reconstruction, and mixed reconstruction. The mixed objective combines the operational structure of PV forecasting with random sequence reconstruction and provides the most balanced performance across forecasting accuracy, degraded NWP conditions, and downstream adaptation. Experiments on 479 distributed PV stations use 340 stations for model development and 139 spatially held-out stations for zero-shot evaluation. Across horizons from 6 hours to 7 days, the multi-site pretrained MR model outperforms representative station-specific and shared baselines, as well as generalist time-series models, including a recent large-scale pretrained foundation model. The pretrained model can also be directly deployed at new PV stations and subsequently adapted to region-specific operational objectives when local data become available, providing a scalable forecasting paradigm for large distributed PV fleets.

infographic.key_insight: A shared, domain-pretrained model forecasts distributed PV generation across sites and horizons, enabling deployment at unseen stations without site-specific retraining.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Fleet-wide forecasting could reduce model training and maintenance while supporting adaptation to local operating needs as station data become available.
method: Formulate forecasting as sequence completion using historical PV power, weather observations, future NWP forecasts, and time encodings.
Pretrain across heterogeneous stations and forecast horizons with forecast-aligned, generic, or mixed reconstruction objectives.
Use mixed reconstruction to balance forecasting accuracy, robustness to degraded NWP, and downstream adaptation.
infographic.evidence_signal: Evaluation covers 479 PV stations—340 for development and 139 spatially held out for zero-shot testing—with reported gains over station-specific, shared, and generalist time-series baselines across 6-hour to 7-day horizons.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical error reductions, so the practical magnitude of gains and performance under local data conditions require verification.
infographic.paper_title: Foundation-Style Pretraining for Scalable and Transferable Distributed PV Forecasting

title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
authors: Qiwei Han, Chi Zhou
abstract: Existing machine-learning models for perovskite solar cells struggle to predict devices made from new materials. Most treat device layers as arbitrary categorical labels and represent perovskite absorbers either through featureless composition vectors or through rigid crystal graphs that require a pre-solved unit cell. As a result, they cannot generalize to unrecorded alloys or unfamiliar cell architectures. We present the Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System (V-PaSS), an architecture built around the physical continuity of perovskite solid solutions. V-PaSS represents arbitrary mixed-cation, mixed-halide absorbers by interpolating relaxed crystal graphs of 23 pure $ABX_3$ endpoint compounds via Vegard's law with learned bandgap bowing. For the device stack, it couples layer sequence and cell polarity (n-i-p or p-i-n) with interfacial band offsets and encodes chemical descriptions with a scientific language model. Evaluated under an institution-grouped protocol where test devices come exclusively from unseen laboratories, an untuned default configuration of V-PaSS achieves the lowest error among fourteen tested models (2.861% MAE, a 5.2% relative reduction over a gradient-boosted baseline at 3.017%, and outperforming the best tuned benchmark at 2.912%). V-PaSS pulls furthest ahead where test devices differ most from training: reducing error by 15.7-19.0% on unseen absorber alloys, by 16.1% on mixed absorbers from new laboratories, and widening its lead over the baseline by 3.6$\times$ on devices with unobserved transport layers. Combined with tree ensembles, V-PaSS sets a new state of the art across all five benchmark splits.

infographic.key_insight: V-PaSS uses physics-aware representations of perovskite alloys and device stacks to improve predictions for unfamiliar solar-cell materials and architectures.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The approach could support screening new absorber compositions and transport-layer combinations without requiring a pre-solved crystal structure for every alloy.
method: Interpolate relaxed crystal graphs of 23 pure ABX₃ endpoints using Vegard’s law and learned bandgap bowing.
Encode layer sequence, cell polarity and interfacial band offsets.
Represent chemical descriptions with a scientific language model.
infographic.evidence_signal: On institution-grouped tests using unseen laboratories, untuned V-PaSS achieved 2.861% MAE versus 3.017% for a gradient-boosted baseline, with 15.7–19.0% error reductions on unseen absorber alloys.
infographic.watch_item: Virtual-alloy interpolation assumes physical continuity; accuracy for compositions that depart from this assumption needs validation.
infographic.paper_title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells

title: Device Model Linking Singlet and Triplet Spin-State Properties to Organic Photovoltaic Device Characteristics
authors: Jun Du, Liming Liu, Jun Yan
abstract: This work proposes an exciton-kinetics coupled drift-diffusion (EKDD) model that bridges device-level charge transport with singlet and triplet excited-state kinetics. State populations and reversible photophysical transitions are solved self-consistently, enabling transient and steady-state device response calculations. We investigate how LE-CT, CT-CS, and LE-T energy offsets, together with triplet-transfer kinetics, govern charge generation, recombination, voltage loss, and extraction in organic photovoltaics. We identify CT-CS offset as a primary, largely overlooked factor controlling charge generation and voltage loss. A positive offset makes CT3-CS separation exothermic and improves generation, but lowers CS energy and increases voltage loss; a negative offset makes separation endothermic and highly temperature-sensitive. The model reproduces triplet-mediated recombination in PM6:Y6 and material-dependent triplet recycling in D18:NFA blends. We propose design rules for balanced generation and voltage loss via two charge-transfer channels: the LE-CT-CS pathway favors a moderate LE-CT offset of about 0.15-0.20 eV and a weakly exothermic CT-CS offset of about 0.05-0.075 eV; the T-CT3-CS pathway requires the same CT-CS alignment plus a small CT-T offset, no more than about 0.1 eV, corresponding to a recycling factor K greater than about 10^-2, to maintain fast T-to-CT3 recycling. CT-CS alignment is the main determinant of the charge-generation-voltage-loss trade-off, while triplet-recycling kinetics determines whether this balance survives at the device level. This work provides a unified theoretical description from exciton generation to free charge collection, offering a convenient tool for transient and steady-state analysis in organic photovoltaics.

infographic.key_insight: Organic photovoltaic performance depends on balancing CT–CS energy alignment for charge generation and voltage loss while maintaining fast triplet recycling.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The model suggests targeting LE–CT offsets of 0.15–0.20 eV, weakly exothermic CT–CS offsets of 0.05–0.075 eV, and CT–T offsets no greater than about 0.1 eV.
method: Couple singlet and triplet exciton kinetics with device drift–diffusion.
Solve state populations and reversible transitions self-consistently.
Calculate transient and steady-state responses across energy offsets and triplet-transfer rates.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports reproduction of triplet-mediated recombination in PM6:Y6 and material-dependent triplet recycling in D18:NFA blends, without quantitative accuracy metrics.
infographic.watch_item: This is a physics-based model, not an AI model; the proposed design ranges require validation across additional materials and operating conditions.
infographic.paper_title: Device Model Linking Singlet and Triplet Spin-State Properties to Organic Photovoltaic Device Characteristics

title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments
authors: Kirill Sobolev, Nagaprasad Reddy Samala, Mariela J. Pavan, Sharon Hazan, Vladimir Ezersky, Shakked Schwartz
abstract: The integration of two-dimensional Ti3C2Tx MXenes into Halide Perovskite (HaP) optoelectronics has shown immense potential for enhancing device performance, yet the fundamental chemical interactions within the precursor ink (a critical stage determining the final material state) remain largely unexplored. This study presents a comprehensive investigation into the chemical stability and surface evolution of Ti3C2Tx MXenes when exposed to the individual and combined components of a model methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI3) solution. By combining detailed X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) analysis with Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations, we decouple the complex interactions between MXenes and the ink constituents. We demonstrate that elemental iodine (I2) and polyiodides (In-) act as aggressive oxidizers, triggering rapid degradation and dissolution of the MXene flakes. Conversely, lead iodide (PbI2) induces a slower oxidation process driven by the strong adsorption of Pb2+ ions onto oxygen terminated sites. In stark contrast, methylammonium iodide (MAI) exhibits a stabilizing effect: it adsorbs onto the MXene surface via hydrogen bonding, effectively passivating the flakes and retarding degradation. In addition, our results reveal that the sequence of precursor addition governs the MXene surface state, requiring extra caution, but also enabling further tunability. These findings provide a critical view on how MXene integration with materials, in general, and HaP in particular, should be perceived, providing a fundamental for their rational engineering.

infographic.key_insight: Ti3C2Tx MXene stability in perovskite precursor inks depends on the constituents and their addition sequence: iodine species accelerate degradation, while methylammonium iodide provides surface passivation.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Controlling precursor chemistry and mixing order could help preserve MXenes during perovskite solar-cell fabrication.
method: Expose MXenes to individual and combined MAPbI3 precursor components.
Use X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to track surface chemical changes.
Apply density functional theory to investigate surface interactions.
infographic.evidence_signal: Combined XPS and DFT findings indicate rapid degradation with iodine/polyiodides, slower oxidation with PbI2, and hydrogen-bond-mediated stabilization with MAI.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract reports precursor-level chemistry, not device-efficiency or operational-lifetime validation; addition sequence requires careful control.
infographic.paper_title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments

title: Domain walls in $R3c$-structured NaNbO$_3$
authors: Jack G. Nedell, Craig J. Fennie
abstract: In this work, we undertake a systematic first-principles study of structural domain walls in the low-temperature rhombohedral $R3c$ phase of perovskite oxide NaNbO$_3$. Employing a group-theoretic classification, we introduce eight unique classes of domain walls in the $R3c$ structure, four of which have a domain wall orientation determined uniquely by the conditions of elastic compatibility and charge neutrality, and perform structural relaxations for each representative domain wall class. We find that one class of 109° domain walls has a notably low energy of 9 mJ m$^{-2}$, comparable to the low-energy ferroelectric walls in BaTiO$_3$. Finally, we find that this class of 109° walls is compatible with the crystal twinning observed in experiments on the $R3c$ phase, and propose an atomistic mechanism for the $R3c \leftrightarrow Pbcm$ phase transition.

infographic.key_insight: First-principles calculations identify a class of 109° domain walls in R3c NaNbO₃ with a notably low energy of 9 mJ m⁻².
infographic.engineering_relevance: These low-energy walls may help explain crystal twinning and structural phase transitions in NaNbO₃, rather than directly inform solar-cell performance.
method: Classify eight unique domain-wall classes using group theory.
Apply elastic-compatibility and charge-neutrality conditions.
Perform first-principles structural relaxations for representative walls.
infographic.evidence_signal: The calculated 109° wall energy is comparable to low-energy ferroelectric walls in BaTiO₃, and this wall class is compatible with experimentally observed twinning.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract proposes an atomistic R3c ↔ Pbcm transition mechanism but reports neither direct experimental validation nor AI or photovoltaic evaluation.
infographic.paper_title: Domain walls in $R3c$-structured NaNbO$_3$

title: Electronic Screening as a Design Lever in La-Doped BaTiO$_3$: Coupled Polarization, Dielectric Response, and Optical Anisotropy
authors: Sikandar Azam, Muhammad Fareed, Qaiser Rafiq, Jan Minar, Abed Alataway
abstract: Donor substitution can tune the coupled ferroelectric, dielectric, electronic, and optical properties of perovskite oxides by modifying lattice distortions and electronic screening. We investigate these effects in La-doped BaTiO3 using density functional theory, density-functional perturbation theory, and the Berry-phase formalism for polarization. For a model with 12.5% La substitution at the Ba site, La incorporation induces anisotropic lattice contraction, reduces tetragonality and Ti off-centering, and weakens the energetic stabilization of the tetragonal ferroelectric phase. The accompanying reduction in polarization is associated with enhanced electronic screening and reduced anomalous Born effective charges. Phonon calculations indicate that the relaxed doped structure is dynamically stable, while hardening of a low-frequency polar mode is consistent with weakened ferroelectricity. The high-frequency dielectric response increases moderately, whereas the static dielectric response decreases as the lattice contribution is suppressed. Electronic-structure calculations show a Fermi-level shift toward the conduction band without mid-gap defect states. The optical spectra exhibit an absorption-edge shift consistent with a Burstein-Moss-type mechanism, enhanced near-edge transparency, and reduced birefringence. Together, these results suggest a microscopic connection between donor-induced screening, polar-mode hardening, reduced dynamical charges, polarization suppression, and decreased optical anisotropy. The conclusions apply to the investigated 12.5% composition; calculations at additional concentrations are needed to establish quantitative doping trends.

infographic.key_insight: At 12.5% La substitution in BaTiO3, enhanced electronic screening is linked to weaker ferroelectric polarization, lower static dielectric response, and reduced optical anisotropy.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Donor substitution offers a potential design lever for balancing ferroelectric, dielectric, and optical properties in perovskite oxide devices.
method: Density functional theory for structural, electronic, and optical properties.
Density-functional perturbation theory for phonons and dielectric response.
Berry-phase calculations of polarization.
infographic.evidence_signal: Calculations indicate a dynamically stable doped structure with reduced Ti off-centering, hardened polar modes, reduced anomalous Born charges, and no mid-gap defect states.
infographic.watch_item: Results cover only 12.5% La substitution; broader doping trends and solar-cell performance are not established.
infographic.paper_title: Electronic Screening as a Design Lever in La-Doped BaTiO$_3$: Coupled Polarization, Dielectric Response, and Optical Anisotropy

title: Symmetry-Based Parameter Efficient Low-Rank Fine-Tuning for High-Throughput Calculation of Lattice Thermal Conductivity
authors: Rustam Arabov, Konstantin Sozykin, Nikita Rybin, Alexander Shapeev
abstract: Accurate and efficient prediction of lattice thermal conductivity (LTC) is essential for developing materials for thermoelectric, microelectronic, and photovoltaic applications. Here, we present a methodology for high-throughput calculation of LTC across large datasets of compounds sharing a common crystal symmetry. Our approach combines fine-tuning of the MatterSim 1M universal machine-learned interatomic potential with LTC calculations based on the solution of the Boltzmann transport equation. We introduce a symmetry-based few-shot fine-tuning strategy (SBFS-FT) based on low-rank adaptation. In this approach, MatterSim 1M is fine-tuned on a small, carefully selected set of compounds that share a common crystal symmetry. The resulting potential is then applicable for accurate LTC calculations for compounds with this crystal symmetry, even if they were not included in the fine-tuning set. We tested our methodology on datasets of half-Heusler compounds (space group 216), materials with space group 225, and spinels (space group 227). We demonstrated that LTC calculations with MatterSim 1M fine-tuned using SBFS-FT exhibited a mean absolute relative difference from the reference results (obtained using moment tensor potentials and polyMLPs) 2-3 times smaller than that achieved with the non-fine-tuned MatterSim 1M potential. Moreover, the accuracy of LTC calculations with MatterSim 1M after SBFS-FT was comparable to that achieved using the MatterSim 1M potentials individually fine-tuned for each compound. Importantly, SBFS-FT enabled generation of the potential suitable for accurate LTC calculations across large compound datasets substantially faster than fine-tuning of MatterSim 1M for each compound individually, reducing the computational time by approximately a factor of 5-7 for a dataset of 100 compounds.

infographic.key_insight: Symmetry-based low-rank fine-tuning of MatterSim 1M enables accurate lattice thermal conductivity predictions across compounds sharing a crystal symmetry without fine-tuning each compound separately.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Faster thermal conductivity screening could support thermal management and materials selection for photovoltaic, microelectronic, and thermoelectric applications.
method: Select a small set of compounds sharing a crystal symmetry.
Fine-tune MatterSim 1M using symmetry-based few-shot low-rank adaptation.
Predict lattice thermal conductivity by solving the Boltzmann transport equation.
infographic.evidence_signal: Across half-Heuslers (space group 216), space-group-225 materials, and spinels (227), the method reduced mean absolute relative differences from reference calculations by 2–3× versus untuned MatterSim 1M, with accuracy comparable to per-compound fine-tuning and approximately 5–7× lower fine-tuning time for 100 compounds.
infographic.watch_item: Transfer was demonstrated within shared-symmetry groups; generalization to other symmetries or improved solar-cell device performance was not established.
infographic.paper_title: Symmetry-Based Parameter Efficient Low-Rank Fine-Tuning for High-Throughput Calculation of Lattice Thermal Conductivity

title: Coupling Evaporation, Chemical Reactions, and Crystallization: A Population-Balance Framework Applied to Two-Step Perovskite Crystallization
authors: K. Segadlo, O. J. J. Ronsin, J. Harting
abstract: A limited understanding of how evaporation couples to crystallization pathways hampers control over the formation of solution-processed perovskite photoactive layers. Identifying these mechanisms-and learning how to select and tune them-is essential for achieving the desired crystal morphology and, ultimately, improving solar-cell performance and stability. To investigate crystallization pathways in evaporating thin films, we develop a simple and general zero-dimensional population-balance model that couples evaporation, chemical reactions, and crystallization. We use the model to explore a range of parameters for a solvent-solute system that follows a two-step crystallization pathway: solvent evaporation first induces formation of a crystalline precursor, which subsequently recrystallizes into the final phase. The model predicts the evolution of the film composition during drying and provides quantitative LaMer curves. Based on these results, we introduce a vocabulary of "supply limitations" and "rate limitations" that enables the interpretation of crystallization kinetics in terms of the governing process conditions.

infographic.key_insight: A zero-dimensional population-balance model links solvent evaporation, chemical reactions, and two-step crystallization to explain how drying conditions govern perovskite phase formation.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The framework could guide drying-process design for controlling perovskite film morphology, with potential relevance to solar-cell performance and stability.
method: Couple evaporation, chemical reactions, and crystallization in a population-balance model.
Explore parameters for crystalline precursor formation followed by recrystallization into the final phase.
Generate film-composition trajectories and quantitative LaMer curves to distinguish supply and rate limitations.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports model-based parameter exploration and predicted drying trajectories, but no experimental validation or device-performance measurements.
infographic.watch_item: The zero-dimensional model does not resolve spatial variations, which may matter when translating predictions to real thin-film processing.
infographic.paper_title: Coupling Evaporation, Chemical Reactions, and Crystallization: A Population-Balance Framework Applied to Two-Step Perovskite Crystallization

title: Climate-Driven Supply-Demand Matching Reshapes Global SolarEV Decarbonization Potential
authors: Yuchen Liu, Stefan Pfenninger-Lee, Tosiyuki Nakaegawa, Takuro Kobashi
abstract: Rooftop photovoltaics (PV) can support rapid urban decarbonization, but their contribution is constrained by the imbalance between PV generation and demand, both shaped by local climate. Growing urban electric-vehicle (EV) deployment creates distributed storage near rooftop PV, shifting PV electricity across time. Here we simulate rooftop PV integrated with EVs as batteries across 5,000 grid cells globally, using hourly meteorology and climate-induced demand. We find that PV-EV systems can supply up to 84% of annual building and mobility electricity demand. Self-sufficiency is highest where daytime demand aligns with generation and seasonal variability remains limited. Using PV capacity factor alone to screen PV-EV potential undervalues 21.9% of the world's 1,000 most populous cities because generation-side metrics overlook the temporal coupling of PV generation, electricity demand and EV storage. Substantial PV-EV potential is concentrated in many low-latitude cities, offering a pathway to cleaner urban energy systems while accelerating progress towards carbon neutrality.

infographic.key_insight: Matching rooftop solar generation with climate-shaped demand and EV battery storage can supply up to 84% of annual building and mobility electricity demand.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Urban PV-EV planning should assess hourly supply-demand alignment and storage flexibility rather than solar capacity factor alone.
method: Simulate rooftop PV integrated with EV batteries across 5,000 global grid cells.
Use hourly meteorology and climate-induced electricity demand.
Assess self-sufficiency and compare capacity-factor screening across the 1,000 most populous cities.
infographic.evidence_signal: The simulations indicate that capacity-factor-only screening undervalues PV-EV potential in 21.9% of the world's 1,000 most populous cities.
infographic.watch_item: Real-world performance depends on EV availability for charging and discharge; the abstract does not establish deployment feasibility or costs.
infographic.paper_title: Climate-Driven Supply-Demand Matching Reshapes Global SolarEV Decarbonization Potential
